questions.question: What is the branch of agriculture called that deals with garden crops - generally fruits, vegetables and ornamental plants?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Horticulture.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Horticulture is the branch of agriculture called that deals with garden crops - generally fruits, vegetables and ornamental plants.**
 
• Horticulture may be defined as the Science and art of growing fruits, vegetables, and flowers, and crops like spices condiments, and other plantation crops.
 
• It is a science of cultivation of Garden plants.
 
• The word Horticulture is derived from the Latin word Hortus meaning garden, and cultura, meaning cultivation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Floriculture:**

 
 
• It may be defined as the branch of horticulture that deals with the culture and management of flowers and ornamental plants.
 
• It has been derived from two words 'flor' means flower and 'cultura' means cultivation.
 
• Floriculture includes the cultivation of flowering and ornamental plants for direct sale or for use as raw materials in the cosmetic and perfume industry and in the pharmaceutical sector.
 
 
 
• **Sericulture:**
 
 
• It is the process of cultivating silkworms and extracting silk from them.
 
• The caterpillars of the domestic silkmoth (also called 'Bombyx Mori) are the most commonly used silkworm species in sericulture.
 
• Other types of silkworms (such as Eri, Muga, and Tasar) are also cultivated for the production of 'wild silks'.
 
 
 
• **Permaculture:**
 
 
• It is an innovative framework for creating sustainable ways of living.
 
• It is a practical method in which ecologically harmonious, efficient and productive systems that can be used by anyone are produced.
 
• It focuses on getting much more out of life by using less.
 
• By this method we can be more productive for less effort, which is also beneficial for our environment and ourselves.
 
• Also its is a method of cooperating with nature and caring for the earth and

 its people.
 
• Permaculture encourages us to be resourceful and self-reliant.

questions.question: Which of the following are non-vascular flowerless plants in the taxonomic division of Bryophyta?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mosses**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mosses**

 
 
• In the taxonomic group of Bryophyta, **mosses are tiny, non-vascular plants without flowers**.
 
• **Bryophyta** is another name for the parent group of **mosses, liverworts, and hornworts known as bryophytes**.
 
• Mosses generally form **dense, green mats or clumps in moist or shaded areas**.
 
• The **simple leaves of individual plants** are often only** one cell thick **and attached to a stem that may or may not have branches.
 
• The stem's function in **transporting water **and nutrients is generally **very limited**.
 
• While **certain species of these plants have conducting tissues**, these are typically underdeveloped and physically distinct from the same tissue seen in vascular plants.
 
• Mosses do **not produce seeds; instead, they produce sporophytes**, which have unbranched stalks and a single capsule bearing spores at the top.
 
• Although other species are significantly larger, they are typically** 0.2–10 cm (0.1–3.9 in) tall**.
 
• The world's tallest moss, **Dawsonia, may reach a** height of 50 cm (20 in). 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bryophyta**

 
 
• The word **"Bryophyta" derives from the Greek words "Bryon" (moss) and "python" (plants)**, respectively.
 
• Embryophytes like **mosses, hornworts, and liverworts **are members of the Bryophyta class.
 
• These are the little plants that flourish** in moist, shaded environments**.
 
• They** don't include vascular tissues**.
 
• Rather than making flowers and seeds, they **reproduce by spores**.
 
• Bryophytes have a **diverse spectrum of morphologies and ecologie**s despite the fact that most do not have complicated tissue organisation.
 
• Although bryophytes are terrestrial plants they need water to complete their life cycle when they reproduce sexually, which is why they are referred to as **"amphibians of the plant kingdom."**

questions.question: What do you call the water holding compounds produced in large quantities by marine brown and red algae?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hydrocolloids**__.

__
 
• Certain marine brown and red algae produce large amounts of **hydrocolloids** (water holding substances), e.g., algin (brown algae), and carrageenin (red algae) are used commercially.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hydrocolloids** are a class of food additives with broad applications in the food industry to develop structure in food ingredients.
 
• **Hydrocolloids** can be synthetic, plant-based, or animal-based. 
 
• Increasing consumer awareness has led to the use of natural food ingredients derived from natural sources, making algae-derived **hydrocolloids** more appealing nowadays. 
 
• **Algae-derived hydrocolloids** such as carrageenan, agar, and alginate are widely used in the food industry as a thickening, gelling, and emulsifying agents. 
 
• **Algae** are the most abundant primary producers, and algae-derived hydrocolloids are high-value thickening, gelling, and emulsifying agents, which have reached **100,000 tons **of annual global production and exceeded **US$ 1.1 billion** of gross market value.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A** lipid** is **any of various organic compounds that are insoluble in water**. They include fats, waxes, oils, hormones, and certain components of membranes and function as energy-storage molecules and chemical messengers.
 
• **Carbohydrates**, or carbs, are **sugar molecules**. Along with proteins and fats, carbohydrates are one of three main nutrients found in foods and drinks. Your body breaks down carbohydrates into glucose.
 
• **Gelatin** is a protein made from animal collagen, usually from cows and pigs. It's commonly used to make capsules, cosmetics, ointments, and foods.

questions.question: Which plant tissue is responsible for the transportation of water and minerals from the soil to the stems and leaves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Xylem**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Xylem:** 

 
 
• This is the **vascular tissue** in **plants** that conducts water and dissolved nutrients upward from the root and also helps to form the woody element in the stem. 
 
• The main function of **xylem **is to **transport water,** but it also transports some nutrients through the plant.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parenchyma:**

 
 
• This is the most common type of **plant tissue **found in the **soft parts of plants.**
 
• It is responsible for the **plant's metabolic functions, such as photosynthesis, storage of starch, fats and oils, and helps in the healing and repair of wounds.**
 
 
 
• **Collenchyma:**
 
 
• This tissue gives support to the plant and is usually found in** layers beneath the epidermis**.
 
• **Collenchyma cells** are elongated cells with thickened cell walls that provide structure and **support for the plant, particularly in regions of new growth**.
 
 
 
• **Phloem:**
 
 
• This is the** living tissue** that transports the** soluble organic compounds made during photosynthesis and known as photosynthates, in particular, sugar, from leaves to the rest of the plant where needed.**
 
• This process is called **translocation**.

questions.question: Which type of plants has weak stems and take support on neighbouring structures to climb up?
questions.solution:
__
 
• Climbers are a group of plants or vines which need the support of some kind as they have weak stems and hence take the support of neighboring structures to climb up.
 
• Some examples of climbers are Money plant, Bougainvillea, Morning glory etc.

 

**Explanation-**__

Plants can be categorized in many ways, including by their size, structure, and other characteristics. A common way is to differentiate them into groups such as trees, shrubs, climbers, and herbs. Here's a basic description of each:

 
• **Trees:** Trees are tall, woody plants usually with a single stem or trunk. They are generally distinguished by their size-typically they are over 10-15 feet tall. Some examples are oak, maple, and pine trees. Trees are an important part of our ecosystems as they provide habitats for a variety of organisms and play a significant role in producing oxygen through photosynthesis.
 
• **Shrubs**: Shrubs, also known as **bushes**, are medium-sized, woody plants. Unlike trees, shrubs typically have several stems and are shorter. They are usually less than 10 feet tall. Examples include holly, lavender, and rose bushes.
 
• **Climbers:** Climber plants, or vines, use support to grow upwards instead of growing erect independently like trees and shrubs. They may attach to structures, and other plants, or use aerial roots to climb. Some climbers like ivy can cover entire buildings or large trees, while others like sweet peas or grapevines are smaller.
 
• **Herbs:** Herbaceous plants or herbs are non-woody, flowering plants. They are generally short-lived and may complete their lifecycle within one or two seasons. They can be annuals (live for one season), biennials (live for two seasons), or perennials (return year after year). Examples include grasses, ferns, wildflowers, and crops such as wheat and rice. In another definition, "herbs" are also plants used in medicine or for seasoning food, such as basil, mint, or rosemary, but these can be trees or shrubs as well.

questions.question: Which type of plants have their branches in the upper part of the stem, much above the ground?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Trees.**

__**Explanation-**__

**Shrubs:** Shrubs are medium-sized, woody plants taller than herbs and have multiple stems. However, they are smaller than trees. Their branches grow near the base, close to the ground and are usually dense and bushy. Examples include azaleas and boxwood.

**Trees: **Trees are the largest plants, and they have a single woody stem or trunk that extends a significant distance above the ground before dividing into branches. The branches of trees primarily grow from the upper part of the stem, well above the ground. Mature trees are typically capable of withstanding all seasons. Examples include oak trees, maple trees, and pine trees.

Herbs: Herbs are small, non-woody and flowering plants. They complete their life cycle in one or two seasons. The term "herb" is also used to describe plants that have medicinal properties or are used for their flavor or scent. Examples include grasses, wheat, and tulips.

questions.question: What is a mushroom?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fungi**__**.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mushroom** is a **Fungi.**
 
• **Scientific Name:** **"Agaricus bisporus"** (Edible Mushroom).
 
• **Scientific Classification of Mushroom:**
 
 
• **Kingdom:** Fungi
 
• **Phylum:** Basidiomycota.
 
 
 
• Any of various fungi having a stalk topped by a **fleshy, often umbrella-shaped cap.**
 
• **Ecology of Mushrooms:**
 
 
• **Sporophores:** The** spore-producing organ** of a fungus or slime mold. **Two types of Sporophores are:**
 
 
• The term **Mushroom** is used to identify the **edible sporophores,**
 
• The term **Toadstool** is often reserved for** inedible or poisonous sporophores. **
 
 
 
• **​Parasites:** Parasites **grow on living trees and other plants, extracting their nutrients.**
 
 
• They are also called the** murderers among the mushrooms.**
 
 
 
• **​Mycorrhiza:** Mycorrhiza **forms a symbiotic association with the roots of living trees.**
 
 
• They take **sugars and nutrients from the tree**, but they **give back minerals and essential elements, enlarging the root system of their hosts.**
 
• **Like, **
 
 
• Porcini Mushrooms, 
 
• Chanterelles, and 
 
• Truffles.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• ​Mushrooms contain **no chlorophyll** which means **they can not photosynthesize.**

questions.question: Which among the following is NOT a micronutrient for plants?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

The essential elements required for plant growth and metabolism are divided into two main categories:

 
• Macronutrients/Macroelements: Macronutrients are generally present in plant tissues in large amounts (in excess of 10 mmole/kg of dry matter)

__
 
• The macronutrients include carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, phosphorous, sulphur, potassium, calcium, and magnesium.

 2.Micronutrients/Microelements: Also called trace elements. These are needed in very small amounts (less than 10 mmole/kg of dry matter)

 
• These include iron, manganese, copper, molybdenum, zinc, boron, chlorine, and nickel

Explanation:__

 
• **Nitrogen** is **not a micronutrient for plants** from the options listed above.
 
• Micronutrients are those elements that are required by the plants in small quantities for their proper functioning.
 
• **Nitrogen** is a **macronutrient**, which means it is required in much larger quantities.
 
• It is a **major component of chlorophyll**, which is the pigment responsible for photosynthesis. It is also a **part of amino acids** which are sub-blocks of proteins in plants.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: The transport of male gametes in Gymnosperms occurs through water.
The transport of male gametes in bryophytes and pteridophytes occurs through water.
The transport of male gametes in bryophytes and pteridophytes occurs through air.
The transport of male gametes in angiosperms occurs through water.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The transport of male gametes in bryophytes and pteridophytes occurs through water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Male gametes** in **both bryophytes and pteridophytes **rely on** water for transportation**.
 
• Produced within antheridia, these male gametes are liberated as free-swimming sperm cells equipped with flagella, enabling them to move through water.
 
• Once released, they navigate to the female reproductive organs for fertilization. Water plays a vital role in the life cycle of bryophytes and pteridophytes, as it facilitates the movement of male gametes.
 
• This dependency on water for reproduction leads to the classification of bryophytes as amphibians of the plant kingdom, emphasizing their need for aquatic environments to complete their life cycle. 
 
• Bryophytes and pteridophytes typically thrive in environments characterized by dampness, shade, and humidity, often found in close proximity to water bodies.
 
• In such habitats, these plants rely on water as a conduit for the movement of their male gametes from the antheridium (male reproductive organ) to the archegonium (female reproductive organ).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Bryophytes** represent a category of land plants, often regarded as a distinct taxonomic division. This group encompasses three main types of non-vascular land plants: liverworts, hornworts, and mosses. Despite lacking vascular tissues for efficient water and nutrient transport, bryophytes play crucial ecological roles in various ecosystems.
 
• **Pteridophytes** are vascular plants that reproduce via spores rather than seeds. They earned the moniker "cryptogams" due to their method of reproduction, which occurs inconspicuously. Pteridophytes include ferns, horsetails, and clubmosses, among others, and they play significant roles in both terrestrial and aquatic habitats.

questions.question:
A coastal area was flooded with sea water and resulted in heavy salt deposits in the nearby area. After a few days, it was observed that many plants died. Based on these statements, which of the following is the most probable cause of the plant deaths?

A. Plants died due to infection from sea water borne germs.

B. Plants died due to absence of sunlight.

C. Plants died due to plasmolysis in the plant cells.

D. Plants died because they were eaten by sea organisms.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plants died due to plasmolysis in the plant cells.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Plasmolysis occurs when plant cells lose water in a hypertonic solution, causing the cell membrane to pull away from the cell wall.
 
• The high salt concentration in the soil creates a hypertonic environment, leading to water loss from the plant cells.
 
• As the water leaves the cells, they become dehydrated and unable to maintain turgor pressure, which is essential for structural integrity and nutrient transport.
 
• This dehydration disrupts vital cellular processes and ultimately results in the death of the plant.
 
• Plasmolysis is a common response to high salinity in the environment, which can be caused by sea water flooding.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hypertonic Solution:**

 
 
• A hypertonic solution has a higher concentration of solutes compared to the inside of the cell.
 
• In a hypertonic environment, water moves out of the cell to balance the solute concentrations, leading to cell shrinkage.
 
 
 
• **Turgor Pressure:**
 
 
• Turgor pressure is the pressure exerted by the cell membrane against the cell wall due to water intake.
 
• It is crucial for maintaining the plant's structural integrity and supporting its upright position.
 
 
 
• **Osmosis:**
 
 
• Osmosis is the movement of water across a semipermeable membrane from an area of low solute concentration to an area of high solute concentration.
 
• It is a vital process for maintaining cellular hydration and nutrient balance.
 
 
 
• **Salinity Stress:**
 
 
• Salinity stress occurs when high salt levels in the soil disrupt the water balance and nutrient uptake in plants.
 
• It can lead to reduced growth, physiological dysfunctions, and even plant death.
